articleTitle: Multi-Channel PA, LNA, and Switch MMICs for Beam-Switching Applications at 160 GHz, Based on an InGaAs mHEMT Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: In this paper, we report 1:8 switch as well as 4-channel low-noise-amplifier (LNA) and power amplifier (PA) circuits, that have been developed for the implementation of Rotman lens-based beam-switching front ends at 160 GHz. The circuits are implemented in an InGaAs-channel metamorphic high-electron mobility transistor (mHEMT) technology with 35-nm gate length. A passive and an active 160-GHz switch variant with 8 dB of insertion loss and 15 dB of gain, respectively, are described. The 4-channel LNA circuit has a noise figure below 3.0 dB, achieving state-of-the-art performance at the lower G-band. Furthermore, more than 14 dBm of linear output power are measured for each channel of the PA circuit, which is state of the art for InGaAs-channel HEMT PA circuits at 160 GHz, featuring more than 18.5 dBm of saturated output power per channel.

articleTitle: Low-Noise Si/SiGe HBT for LEO Satellite User Terminals in Ku-Ka Bands
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper discusses technological choices and resulting performances of an innovative Si/SiGe HBT architecture developed for a new 55-nm BiCMOS platform from STMicroelectronics targeting LEO satellites user terminals application in Ku-Ka bands. Transistor architecture has been designed to combine a low-noise performance with a cost-effective technology (for high-volume production), that are two major requirements for LEO satellite user terminals. Collector integration is widely simplified compared to previous BiCMOS technologies developed by STMicroelectronics taking advantage of ion implantation capabilities. Low-noise performance is addressed by a new generation of emitter-base architecture featuring an epitaxial base link, reducing the base resistance. Record noise performances are demonstrated with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$NF_{\text{MIN}}\sim$</tex> 0.6-dB at 20 GHz at device level and 1.13-dB at 11.85 GHz at circuit (packaged receiver) level associated to a gain of ~28dB. SiGe HBT also features −390 GHZ <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_\mathrm{T}$</tex> and −500-GHz <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_\text{MAX}$</tex>

articleTitle: A 19-dB Peaking at 72-GHz and 4.1-Vppd Output Swing SiGe BiCMOS Linear Driver with Dynamic Cascode Output Buffer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: As symbol rate increases over 100 GBd in digital coherent optical communication system, high-frequency loss compensation becomes a critical issue. This paper presents a 4-ch lumped linear driver IC with 19-dB peaking at 72 GHz, variable by over 6 dB, which is favorable for high-frequency loss compensation. Low frequency gain is 25 dB at maximum and variable by over 18 dB, which is beneficial for compensating amplitude decrease caused by de-emphasis. P1dB is over 4-Vppd from 1 to 50 GHz. A novel open collector output buffer with a dynamic cascode and series inductors realized such large peaking and excellent linearity. Designed by 55-nm SiGe BiCMOS technology, the driver IC integrates a control circuit with serial peripheral interface (SPI) compliant with optical internetworking forum (OIF) standard and the power dissipation is 0.54 W/ch including the control circuit. A coherent driver modulator (CDM) assembled with this driver IC shows 9.7 % error vector magnitude (EVM) with 128-GBd single polarization 16 quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) operation under back-to-back configuration.

articleTitle: Multi-Finger 250-nm InP/GaAsSb DHBTs with Record 37.3 % Class-A PAE at 94 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: We report the first DC, RF, and W-band large-signal power performance of multi-finger 250-nm InP/GaAsSb DHBTs for power amplifier applications at mm- and sub-mm-wave frequencies. Two- and four-finger DHBTs in either common-emitter (CE) or common-base (CB) configuration are fabricated with 7.5- and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10-\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> -long emitter fingers. A 94 GHz InP HBT record measured class-A power-added efficiency PAE = 37.3 % is achieved with two-finger CB-HBTs. A saturated output power POUT, SA <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{T}=15\ \text{dBm}$</tex> is measured with both the four-finger CE- and CB-DHBT structures. The high cut-off frequencies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(f_{\mathrm{T}/}f_{\text{MAX}}\approx 500/760$</tex> GHz) and superior power properties of InP/GaAsSb multi-finger DHBTs highlight their attractiveness for sub-mm-wave power amplifiers (PAs).

articleTitle: Microstrip and Grounded CPW Calibration Kit Comparison for On-Wafer Transistor Characterization from 220 GHz to 325 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the effect of two calibration errors, probe placement and capacitance per unit length, on transistor characterization, from 220 GHz to 325 GHz, on both a microstrip and an inverted coplanar waveguide with a via-stitched ground plane (CPW-G) calibration kit. We find that the calibration errors tend to be greater for the microstrip calibration than for the CPW-G calibration. These findings have critical ramifications for transistor characterization and modelling, and active circuit design.

articleTitle: Numerical Device Simulation Aided Study of RF-Stress-Caused Degradation in SiGe HBTs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: TCAD simulations of an advanced SiGe HBT are performed with and without considering the impact of compressive lattice strain on the effective density of states and on the carrier mobility. Relaxation of compressive lattice strain is discussed as a possible physical cause of the collector current degradation in SiGe HBTs that has been experimentally observed in previously reported RF stress tests.

articleTitle: Fully Qualified Gallium Nitride Power Amplifier for Use in Ka-Band Commercial Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: There is a need for Solid State Power Amplifiers (SSPA's) to be used in High Throughput Satellites (HTS) for commercial applications. Specifically when the amount of information passed through the transponders, i.e. capacity, is determined mainly by the quantity of beams the satellite can generate. This application is well suited for SSPA's over the conventional TWTA solution as they are smaller and lighter weight enabling a simplification of HTS payload architectures, higher density physical integration, and the ability to support active array transmit solutions all of which increases the quantity of beams and thus capacity. More specifically, Gallium Nitride (GaN) Power Amplifiers (PA's) have shown the ability to generate high RF output power levels with small size and high efficiency thereby enabling step function improvement in capacity [1], [2]. This paper will describe a 20GHz fully space qualified GaN PA module developed for KaBand commercial satellite downlinks. The design techniques, test results, and screening regimen required to meet the demanding performance and reliability requirements will be given. The result is a 20GHz module with >55dB of gain, >10W of Pout, >30% peak PAE, and NPR >15dB. To the authors knowledge this is the best fully space-qualified module performance at this frequency published to date.

articleTitle: Modeling of the Snappy, and Soft Reverse Recovery of SiC MOSFET's Body Diode
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: Different reverse recovery modes of the SiC MOSFET's body diode are investigated in this paper. Using semiconductor device simulation, the operating conditions under which snappy, and soft reverse recovery occur in power electronics applications are better explained. The work presented here verifies that the snappy or soft recovery is dependent on the dynamic carrier distribution in the drift region during reverse bias. The Compact Modeling Coalition (CMC) p-i-n diode model is used to model the body diode of SiC MOSFET because it contains the requisite equations and parameters for the dynamic distribution of carriers. The physics-based model includes parameters for bias-dependent depletion layer, separate anode and cathode injection, and non-quasi-static charge distribution. Consequently, the model permits simulation of the snappy, and soft reverse recovery of the body diode based on external circuit conditions. The paper verifies the model by comparing simulation results to measured switching data at various temperatures, and gate resistances. This modeling exercise can facilitate the power electronics system's optimal design.

articleTitle: Thermal Characterization of InP/GaAsSb DHBTs: Effect of Emitter and Collector Layers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: Modern telecommunication systems require transistors that can deliver high power levels at high frequencies. This poses challenges for the reliability of transistors operating close to their peak performance. The thermal behavior of mm-wave InP/GaAsSb DHBTs is studied for several emitter contact widths and lengths, and various epitaxial design alternatives are considered. The effect of the emitter and collector layer stacks is reported. Straightforward modifications to the GaInAs sub-collector contact thickness and composition significantly reduce the thermal resistance R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf> and junction temperature. We show that a thin emitter yields similar thermal improvements in characteristics as improvements made to the collector design.

articleTitle: An 18.6-dBm, 8-Way-Combined D-Band Power Amplifier with 21.6% PAE in 22-nm FD-SOI CMOS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents a 2-stage, 8-way power-combined fully depleted silicon-on-insulator (FDSOI) CMOS power amplifier (PA) operating from 110–125 GHz. An optimal power combining strategy realizes high power-added efficiency (PAE) with 8 pseudo-differential stages power cells matched approximately to 50 Ohms. Additionally, low-loss output matching networks improve PAE using sub-quarter wavelength (SQWL) coupled-line baluns (CLB). Fabricated in 22-nm FD-SOI CMOS technology, the PA generates 18.6-dBm saturated output power <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(P_{sat})$</tex>, 21.6% peak PAE at 18.2-dBm, and occupies 0.183 mm 2 core area. The power density is 0.4 W/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>•

articleTitle: A Wideband Ultra-Low Noise 15–55 GHz Dual-Beam Receive Phased-Array Beamformer with 2.9-4.2 dB NF
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents an 8-channel 15–55 GHz dual-beam receive (Rx) phased-array beamformer in 90 nm SiGe BiCMOS process capable of synthesizing two simultaneous beams at any frequency. The design achieves ultra-low noise figure in the 15–55 GHz band together with high linearity per element. Each channel also has a 5-bit phase control and 22 dB gain control. The outputs of the 4 channels for the two beams are combined using two independent Wilkinson networks. The measured chip has an electronic gain of 25 dB with a NF of 2.9-4.2 dB at 15–50 GHz, and an IP1dB of −31±3 dBm. To the authors' knowledge, this work achieves the lowest NF for wideband Rx beamformers in the same frequency range. The chip also demonstrates an EVM of < 2.5% at 25–42 GHz for 5G 400 MHz OFMD waveforms with a PAPR of 11.6 dB. Application areas are phased-arrays covering multiple 5G bands and multi-standard systems.

articleTitle: Transient Field-Plate Thermometry in Cascode FET Power Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: Transient field-plate thermometry is demonstrated on cascode FET S-band and X-band GaN power amplifiers. Mesa thermometry is also demonstrated on the same amplifiers and compared to the field-plate data. A transient thermal model is proposed for both field-plate and mesa thermometry that agrees well with measured data. This is the first published study of thermal transients in cascode (stacked-FET) power amplifiers.

articleTitle: D-Band Power Amplifier with 27 dBm Peak Output Power and 14.9% PAE in 250-nm InP HBT Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: We present a D-band power amplifier (PA), implemented in Teledyne (TSC)-250-nm InP technology, that produces 27.2dBm output power and 14.9% associated PAE at 150 GHz. The measured saturated output power exceeds 26 dBm over 126–150 GHz. The output stage power-combines sixteen <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f4-\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> common-base cells, each having capacitive series feedback that increases the real part of the input impedance, reducing inter-stage matching losses. Each power cell is independently biased by an adaptive bias network that prevents thermal runaway and increases bias currents with increased RF power to maintain nearly constant gain. The IC consumes 3 mm2.

articleTitle: Demonstration of a Ku-Band N-Path Downconverter in GaN-on-SiC
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents a Ku-band, interference tolerant downconverter based on N-path passive mixers implemented in GaN-on-SiC process. The mixer-first topology employs sinusoidal quadrature LO, but includes a transformer-based splitter between I and Q mixers to reduce loss due to LO overlap in the mixers. At 17 GHz, the circuit achieves a measured in-band conversion loss of 9.5dB, out-of-band blocker-induced input 1-dB gain compression (OOB B1dB) of 10.4 dBm and input third-order intercept point (OOB IIP3) of 21.8 dBm. The chip takes in 11 dBm of LO input power which translates to a competitive linear efficiency of 10.8 dB. The downconverter maintains its loss and linearity properties across 15.5-18.5 GHz. The chip's integrated LO buffers consume 32 mA at 8 V supply and occupies 2.06mm x 1.26mm die area only. To the best of authors' knowledge, this is the first demonstration of N-path passive mixers in GaN technology in RF/mmWave frequencies.

articleTitle: A D-Band Sub-Harmonically Pumped Mixer with High LO Suppression Using 250-nm InP DHBT P-N Junction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper reports the prototyping and experimental results of the 150 GHz sub-harmonically pumped up-conversion mixer using 250-nm InP DHBT anti-parallel P-N junction. The junction size is optimized for minimizing the intermodulation distortion. The measured conversion loss of 15 dB, the 3rd order input intercept point of +5 dBm and RF to LO suppression of more than 20 dB are obtained. It shows the InP DHBT's potential use of passive mixer without inter-stage filter for the higher functionalities integration.

articleTitle: The Impact of BEOL Stress on SiGe HBTs at Cryogenic Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: To support the use of SiGe heterojunction bipolar transistors (UBTs) in cryogenic environments such as space or quantum computing readout, the temperature dependence of back-end-of-line (BEOL) induced mechanical stress effects was investigated from 300 K to 13 K. Test structures with 9 metal layers placed directly above the device were used to introduce BEOL stress in the SiGe HBT. Measurements and simulations show a substantial increase in sensitivity to BEOL stress at cryogenic temperatures. This increase is attributed to a combination of the higher slope of the Gummel characteristics with cooling and higher overall stress caused by thermal mismatch. Increasing the distance of the metal stack from the active device was simulated to help determine the region in which BEOL stress effects are significant. For circuits intended to operate at cryogenic temperatures, designers should ensure identical BEOL routing around devices sensitive to mismatch.

articleTitle: An 80-GBaud PAM-4 $G_{\mathrm{m}}$ -Boosted Variable-Gain TIA in 22-nm FDSOI
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: A variable-gain transimpedance amplifier (VG-TIA) with over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$80-\text{dB}\Omega$</tex> differential <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z_{21}$</tex> and over 45 dB of gain control, 36-GHz bandwidth, operating at record symbol and data rates of up to 80 GBaud PAM-4 and 160 Gb/s, respectively, is presented. The differential multi-stage TIA features a 6-mA, 53- <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{dB}\Omega\ g_{\mathrm{m}}$</tex> -boosted cascode input stage with 70-GHz bandwidth which minimizes the differential input equivalent noise and input impedance, making its bandwidth less sensitive to the PIN photodiode capacitance, while simultaneously providing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$59-\Omega$</tex> input impedance per side for ease of on-die testing without a photodiode. A double-cascode Gilbert-Cell VGA and two fixed-gain Cherry-Hooper stages provide the extra 25 dB of gain and help maintain the THD below 3 % for differential input currents up to 4.8 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{mA}_{\text{pp}}$</tex>. The equivalent input noise current remains below 21.4 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{pA}/\sqrt{}\text{Hz}$</tex> up to 50 GHz.

articleTitle: GaN and GaAs HEMT Channel Charge Model for Nonlinear Microwave and RF Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: An explicit HEMT channel-charge compact model is developed that describes both energy-conserving and transit charge components in GaN and GaAs HEMTs. Uniquely and significantly, a charge formation-energy function is developed that defines the conserved component. A non-conserved component is identified, which is a transit charge that produces a mutual capacitance.

articleTitle: Gen1 Active Tunable SiGe Integrated Parallel Synthesis Filters (PSF) without Q-Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents a proof of concept of high-order LC tunable filters without Q-enhancement in a SiGe BiCMOS process using a parallel synthesis approach. By manipulating the parallel resonators phase properties, a 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>-order band-pass filter is synthesized using subtraction of the two LC-resonators. Despite the on-chip low-Q passives, a wide center-frequency tuning, a large 3-dB tunable bandwidth, and high out-of-band attenuation is achieved. The presented filter is center-frequency tunable from 7 to 11 GHz with a constant 3-dB bandwidth of 1.5 GHz. Additionally, the filter bandwidth can also be tuned from 850 MHz to 1800 MHz. The proposed filter offers a competitive performance, typically suitable for RF receive chain after a low-noise amplifier, in terms of in-band IIP3 of -2 to +3 dBm, NF of 11 to 12 dB, fixed power consumption of 33.6 mW, a highly integrated small form factor, frequency and bandwidth tunability, all without the need for any positive feedback Q-enhancement circuit. Other features of the proposed filter are switched-varactor controls for high linearity, on-chip passive baluns, continuous tuning offering a high number of filter states to the system, simple control, and compatibility with existing digital controller. The proposed filter is implemented in Tower Semiconductor 180 nm SiGe BiCMOS process to achieve higher integration of phased-arrays common receive module at Northrop Grumman Mission Systems and further enables imaging radar, EW and SIGINT systems tunability.

articleTitle: Physics-Based Compact Modeling of the Transfer Current in III-V DHBTs with the Generalized Integral Charge Control Relation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: Physics-based modeling of the transfer current of III-V DHBTs (Double Heterojunction Bipolar Transistors) using the Generalized Integral Charge-Control Relation (GICCR) is discussed. The impact of selected material properties on the transfer current is analyzed based on TCAD simulations and the GICCR. Based on the insights obtained from this analysis, an improved formulation of the transfer current is suggested and verified using measurement data of an InP/GaAsSb DHBT and an InP/InGaAs DHBT technology.

articleTitle: 100 GBaud DSP-Free PAM-4 Optical Signal Generation Using an InP-DHBT AMUX-Driver and a Thin-Film Lithium Niobate Modulator Assembly
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: In this article, we report on the generation of 100-GBd (200-Gb/s) 4-level pulse-amplitude modulation (PAM-4) optical signal, without any support of digital signal processing (DSP) nor off-line equalisation. This is achieved in using an uncooled indium phosphide (InP) analog-multiplexer (AMUX)-driver and a thin film lithium niobate (TFLN) Mach-Zehnder modulator (MZM) assembly, with a -3-dB electro-optical bandwidth in excess of 85 GHz. This result paves the way for low-power DSP-free beyond-1-Tb/s transceivers for next generation optical communication systems and 6G applications. We also present the design and characterisation of the AMUX-driver integrated circuit (IC). The InP-DHBT IC shows a 2-Vppd output swing at 100 GBd in PAM-4 while operating at a 100-GSa/s sampling-rate.

Author Keywords: Indium Phosphide (InP) double heterojunction bipolar transistor (DHBT)

articleTitle: Analog/mmWave Circuit Demonstrations in State-of-the-Art SiGe BiCMOS Process for 5G and Optical Transceivers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: In this invited paper, measured results of four different analog/mmWave circuits with excellent figures-of-merit (FoM) are demonstrated in SiGe technologies. First, a low noise amplifier (LNA) with very high gain of 19.1 dB and NF of 1.3 dB at 19 GHz for SATCOM is demonstrated. A mmWave cascode power cell having an excellent Psat of 17 dBm with 45% PAE at 47 GHz is shown. SiGe npn ring oscillator (RO) with very low delay of 2.59 ps using tail current of 3.57 mA is demonstrated. Finally, performance of transimpedance amplifiers (TIA) is compared across two different SiGe Technologies using measurements. Excellent agreement with simulations is demonstrated in the case of LNA and TIA.

articleTitle: 46–102 GHz GaN Balanced Cascode Amplifier-Isolator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper details a solid-state transistor isolator using a balanced cascode amplifier topology. The circuit design, with a focus on stability, is discussed. The amplifier is implemented in a 40nm GaN-on-SiC process with an overall size of 2.1mm by 1.6 mm. Measured small-signal S-Parameters are in good agreement with simulation with a flat <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{21}$</tex> of 7 dB over a 3-dB bandwidth of 46 GHz to 102 GHz. Reverse isolation is above 32 dB over this frequency range. Large-signal measurements from 82 GHz to 96 GHz show a 1 dB input compression point between 5–6 dBm with corresponding output power up to 13.7 dBm. The presented circuit is well suited for use in wideband millimeter-wave MMIC front ends, as e.g. an isolated driver.

articleTitle: A High Linearity SiGe D-Band Diode Ring Mixer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: Although the SNR and thus the maximum range of FMCW radar systems benefit from high output powers, they can conventionally be limited by the receiver linearity. As a solution, we propose a fully integrated diode-based down-conversion ring mixer designed in Infineon's B11HFC 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS technology. Excellent port isolation allows this architecture to be used throughout the D-band up to the power range substantially exceeding the state-of-the-art. The mixer exhibits a measured, maximum 1dB compression point of 11.9 dBm and a minimum voltage loss of 1.1dB. Complemented by a matching network and optimized for connection to an operational amplifier, it represents a competitive alternative to conventional, active approaches.

articleTitle: Practical Approaches to Industrializing Near-THz Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: In the past few years we have seen the proliferation of mm-Wave & sub-6GHz communication radios due to the global effort to make ultra-high capacity 5G a reality. Such systems benefit not only from RFIC innovations, but also from packaging, material engineering and co-design of various elements to produce scalable and manufacturable products. While near-THz communication systems may not be initially considered for mobility applications, they are poised to offer unprecedented capacity for backhaul links reaching 100Gb/s. Furthermore, applications such as imaging, high-resolution radar & instrumentation continue to benefit from advancements in near-THz systems. This plenary talk focuses on practical approaches to enable manufacturing of near-THz modules at scale, and at a price-point suitable for mass deployment. This plenary talk presents various feature-rich RFICs, packaging and interposer technology operating at E-Band (71-86GHz) & D-Band (110GHz - 170GHz) which are capable of achieving tens of gigabit per second at high spectral efficiency and output power.

articleTitle: 120 GHz GaAs Single-Balanced Mixer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents a resistive down-conversion single-balanced mixer in WIN semiconductor's 0.1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \text{mGaAs}$</tex> process. This mixer operates within the low terahertz region up to a frequency of 120 GHz. The measured upper-side band conversion loss is lower than 12.2 dB up to 115 GHz and lower than 14.4 dB up to 120 GHz at a fixed LO frequency of 110 GHz. The LO-RF isolation of the mixer is further enhanced using a selective drain biasing technique, which is demonstrated for the first time in the low terahertz region. The article also includes the first demonstration of phase and magnitude imbalances between the two output IF signals at these low terahertz frequencies, which are measured to be less than 7.6° and 0.41 dB, respectively, within an IF frequency range of 1–8 GHz.

articleTitle: Design Trade-offs between Series-Peaking Inductor and High $f_T$ SiGe HBTs in Transimpedance Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: Series-peaking inductor is a crucial block in a shunt-feedback Transimpedance amplifier (TIA) used for bandwidth enhancement. Achieving high-quality factor (Q) and high self-resonant frequency (SRF) of on-chip inductors is challenging for large bandwidth TIAs. A higher <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_T$</tex> heterojunction bipolar transistor (HBT) can relax the requirement of series-peaking inductance. Due to the lower inductance value, a high <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> and high SRF can be achieved. This paper presents design trade-offs between the series-peaking inductor and HBT device parameters using two different GlobalFoundries SiGe BiCMOS processes 9HP+ (90nm Bulk) and 45nm SiGe (45nm RFSOI). The simulation and measurement results are shown to validate the trade-offs. Measurements show that 45nm SiGe TIAs have 15-25% more bandwidth than 9HP+ TIAs, with a 14-30% reduction in inductance across various device sizes.

articleTitle: Wideband Switched-Capacitor and Switched-Transmission-line Circulators in 40nm GaN Technology: Design and Device Modeling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents broadband circulators based on switched capacitor and switched transmission-line architectures implemented in a 40nm Gallium Nitride (GaN) process. Using GaN HEMT as a switch enhances the power handling of these architectures achieving an IPldB of 9/12dBm, representing an 8/11dB increase over wideband CMOS circulators demonstrated in the past. The switched-transmission-line architecture enhances bandwidth by eliminating the charge/discharge of capacitors. The operating frequency range is DC-1.1GHz for this architecture for a 100MHz clock frequency. The DC insertion loss is 2.2dB/3dB for the switched T-line and switched capacitor architecture and matching and isolation are better than < −15dB, and > 18dB for both the architectures within the respective operating frequency ranges. One primary design challenge is the lack of all-region models for GaN transistors, particularly for switch configuration. This paper develops a virtual-source model for the 40nm GaN HEMTs and shows the agreement between measurements and simulations.

articleTitle: Vertical Power Delivery and Heterogeneous Integration for High-Performance Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents a heterogeneously integrated vertical power delivery (power tree) system that combines a 180nm HV BCD 20V:4V hybrid converter, a 65nm 4V:1V switched-capacitor converter, and an interposer filled with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\mathrm{D}$</tex> nano-porus deep-trench flying and decoupling capacitors. A prototype of the overall system achieves a total efficiency of 87% from 20V to 0.9V, all while featuring high-voltage vertical delivery that minimizes lateral conduction losses and the total number of pins required for power/ground.

articleTitle: GaN/Si 37–40 GHz T/R Chip MMIC for 5G Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents a Transmit/Receive chip MMIC intended for 5G applications. The circuit is implemented and fabricated using a 100nm Gallium Nitride on Silicon (GaN/Si) millimeter wave process. The T/R chip is designed in the 37-40GHz operating frequency band and integrate two RF SPDT switches, Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) and Power Amplifier (PA) in the same chip. The MMIC, including the RF switch losses exhibit in Rx mode a gain of 15dB and NF less than 3.5dB withing a power consumption of 330mW. In Tx mode, the T/R chip shows a gain of 27dB at 39GHz, an average output power of 35dBm and Power Added Efficiency (PAE) of 17% at 39GHz. Despite the MMIC integrates two SPDT switches to reduce the number of RF port accesses (only two ports here instead usually three ports), the circuit is compact and the size does not exceed 3.1x3mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> which is less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda/2$</tex> at 40GHz, allowing better integration with microstrip patch antenna array used in 5G communication system.

articleTitle: The SiGe HBT at Cryogenic Temperatures: Invited Pager
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: The operation of SiGe HBTs down to temperatures as low as the mK quantum regime is reviewed. Motivation and history, operative transport physics, simulation and modeling, issues requiring special attention, as well as emerging applications, are all addressed.

articleTitle: High-Speed SiGe BiCMOS Circuits for Optical Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents an overview of SiGe BiCMOS circuits for next-generation optical communication links targeting 100 GBd PAM4 modulation per wavelength to support 4-lane 800Gb and 8-lane 1.6Tb Ethernet. Signal generation at these rates is challenging. For this, an analog multiplexer making use of return-to-zero (RZ) modulation is presented. The explicit RZ generation enables equalization of the interleaved signal. Higher equalization orders are obtained with a 120 GBd PAM4 4-to-1 multiplexer with a mixed-signal 7-tap feedforward equalizer. The equalizer consists of a combination of digital delay cells and analog delay cells enabling a compact and power efficient solution. Quad-channel modulator drivers and receivers finish the required high-speed circuits. Based on traveling-wave architectures high gain-bandwidth products are realized.

articleTitle: High Performance $0.25\mu\mathrm{m}$ GaN Technology with Low Memory Effects
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: Gallium nitride (GaN) heterostructure field effect transistor (HFET) technology have become the main stream solution for RF communication infrastructure applications for 5G networks and beyond. This paper presents a 0.25 μm gate length delivering gain and efficiency improvements along with superior reliability and without compromising our low memory differentiation. The technology delivers 10 W/mm power density and 79% drain efficiency at 3.5 GHz while maintaining strong drain lag performance over temperature. A Doherty amplifier based on this technology delivers 56-59% efficiency, >16 dB gain over the 3.4-3.8 GHz band under a 20 MHz L TE signal with 38.5 dBm average output power with >16 dB gain. RF Intrinsic reliability tests predict> 1e7 hr. MTTF with < 0.01 FITs at 225°C.

articleTitle: A Novel Base Resistance Model Incorporating Base Distributive Effects Along with Emitter Length
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: The base resistance is a critically important parameter for bipolar transistors. Base contact width and thickness can limit the maximum emitter length that can be used in a power amplifier application. This paper presents a novel scalable base resistance model; the concept of a characteristic length to define the base resistance distributive effect along the emitter length is proposed. The new base model is in good agreement with that from traditional compact model extraction approach using extensive data set analysis and an intensive fitting algorithm. In addition, this new distributed base resistance model is based on physical electrical current mechanism, it has much better scalability for device geometries, process and material parameter changes. It also provides a guidance in the optimization of the device design. device layout. and base metallization process.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Gallium Nitride Maturation of 40nm T3 Gallium Nitride Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit Process
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: Future microelectronics systems will rely on gallium nitride (GaN) devices able to operate at higher frequencies. Smaller gate length nodes enable such applications but have their own manufacturing challenges. HRL Laboratories offers a 40nm T3 GaN process with fT and fmax of 160/360GHz, power density up to 2W/mm, and noise figure of 1.8dB at 94GHz. Under internal and DARPA funding, this process has been matured for improved performance, yield, and cycle time. The process is monitored through three standard evaluation circuits covering X-, Ka-, and W-band and their performance correlates well with pulsed-current measurements. HRL has also matured the metal-embedded chiplet assembly for microwave integrated circuit (MECAMIC) technology and built demonstration circuits.

articleTitle: A 202 GHz Link Using Planar Transceiver Modules
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: We report a 202 GHz wireless data transmission link, communicating 32 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Gb}/\mathrm{s}$</tex> over 7.1 meters, using planar InP HBT transmitter and receiver modules. The modules are highly integrated and require simple physical assembly without waveguide interfaces. A single 2.8 mm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times\ 0.75$</tex> mm InP HBT transmitter IC and a single 2.3 mm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times\ 0.85$</tex> mm InP HBT receiver IC, operating from a 24.5 GHz local oscillator (LO) reference, provide frequency conversion between 6 GHz (I, Q) intermediate-frequency (IF) and the 202 GHz modulated carrier. Signals are radiated and received by directly wire-bonding the InP ICs to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2$</tex> patch antenna arrays on 50 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>substrates, with these antennas coupled to external 50 mm diameter PTFE lenses. 8 Gbaud 16QAM data transmission (32 Gb/s) over 7.1 m, on a link with 10.4 dB added attenuation, showed 13.4% RMS error vector magnitude.

articleTitle: A Physically-Based Matching Model for HiSIM_HV
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents a physically-based matching model that incorporates mismatch fluctuations into the HiSIM_HV MOSFET model. Analytical expressions capturing variations in threshold voltage, current factor, and drift region resistor have been developed and integrated into the compact model. The proposed model accurately predicts drain current mismatch across a wide operational range while utilizing just three matching parameters. Validation was performed through Monte Carlo simulations, which were compared against experimental measurements on diverse device classes fabricated using X-FAB's 0.18 µm processes. The results encompass drain current mismatch, standard deviation of threshold voltage, and standard deviation of the current factor. The presented outcomes demon-strate good agreement between measurements and simulations.

articleTitle: The Effects of Carbon Doping on the Performance and Electrical Reliability of SiGe HBTs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: The effects of carbon doping in the SiGe base on the electrical reliability of SiGe HBTs are investigated. This study uses three separate SiGe HBTs, each with an identical process flow with the exception of the carbon dose introduced during the SiGe epitaxial growth. These devices are characterized for open-base collector-emitter breakdown voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$BV_{CEO}$</tex> and open-emitter collector-base breakdown voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$BV_{CBO}$</tex>, which are relevant predictors of device voltage handling. Electrical stress was then performed to investigate damage trends with aging. It is shown that the increase in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$BV_{CEO}$</tex> with increasing carbon content is a result of a decrease of peak DC current gain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex>, and not of any carbon-dependent change in the damage mechanisms. It is also shown that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$BV_{CBO}$</tex> and multiplication factor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M-1$</tex> do not change with carbon, indicating similar impact-ionization for all profiles. It was also shown that, although the magnitude of base current near operating bias is highest after stress for the highest-carbon device, the relative shift is lower due in part to the existence of pre-stress traps from in-situ carbon.

articleTitle: 3D Heterogeneous Integration (3DHI): An Enabler For Next Generation RF Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: To perform increasingly diverse missions in increasingly crowded electromagnetic (EM) environments, future sensor and communication systems will require increased bandwidth, sensitivity and enhanced functionality per unit area. These needs are driving sensor arrays towards higher levels of integration of a diverse set of materials, devices and components across multiple domains. This includes 3D solutions, particularly at millimeter wave and THz frequencies. This talk will present an overview of the evolution of heterogenous integration programs at DARPA and potential paths forward, including innovations in millimeter wave components and architectures being developed in the ELectronics for G-band ARrays (ELGAR) program, thermal management of high-power density and 3D electronics (THREADS and MiniTherms3D) and 3DHI at the transistor level being explored under the Heterogeneous Heterostructures (H2) and related programs.

articleTitle: High Volume Wafer Fab Equipment for RF Technologies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This overview paper describes functional components that make up a typical RF system and the high-volume semiconductor manufacturing tools used to produce them. As an example, a simplified SiGe BiCMOS RF process flow is presented, and 300mm semiconductor processing modules and tools needed for the manufacturing of this RF-focused process are described.

articleTitle: A DC-to-150-GHz InP-DHBT Active Combiner Module for Ultra-Broadband Signal Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents an active combiner module with the widest bandwidth ever reported. In the module, a wideband combiner IC fabricated in 250-nm InP DHBT is implemented. The IC uses a distributed topology with separated output transmission lines and a multi-peaking method to widen the bandwidth and to compensate for packaging loss. The IC achieved a bandwidth of 220 GHz with an over-5-dB peaking gain. It was mounted on a quartz-based substrate by flip-chip bonding and implemented with 0.8-mm coaxial connectors. The combiner module achieved a unity gain with a bandwidth of 150 GHz, the widest ever reported. It also successfully demonstrated interleaving of two-band signals in a range from DC to 113 GHz.

articleTitle: A 61-187.2-GHz Traveling Wave Push-Push Frequency Doubler in a 130 nm SiGe:C BiCMOS Technology With 101.7% Fractional Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents a differential, distributed frequency doubler using the Traveling Wave Principle for wideband operation. Three push-push stages, which are evenly distributed within two input transmission lines and one output transmission line, are employed in a proposed frequency doubler. The proposed doubler attains a 6 dB-bandwidth of 126.2 GHz, encompassing four frequency bands: the entire W- and D-band, and partially extending into the E-band and G-band. The maximum measured output power is -0.48dBm at the doubled frequency of 93 GHz. Furthermore, the fractional bandwidth of 101.7% surpasses the state of the art regardless of the technology employed.

articleTitle: A 12–162 GHz Distributed Amplifier in a 45-nm BiCMOS SOI Process Achieving 2.67 THz Gain-Bandwidth Using an Active Bias Termination
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: A low power 12–162 GHz distributed amplifier (DA) is demonstrated with an average gain of 25 dB. This circuit is realized with a NMOS/HBT cascode cell using a 45-nm BiCMOS Silicon-on-Insulator (SOI) process. The DA utilizes the high <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{f}_{\max}$</tex> CMOS to provide an active bias termination on the input in order to add tunability in the circuit to mitigate the unknowns of a new process. The total power consumption of the DA is 215 mW with a core area of 0.45 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{mm}^{2}$</tex>.

articleTitle: A 4–18 GHz, 35 W GaN MMIC Power Amplifier with Improved Thermal Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: The design and measured performance of a non-uniform distributed power amplifier (NDPA) operating from 4 to 18 GHz and achieving an output power of 35 W with an associated PAE between 25 % and 33 % is demonstrated. This design utilizes a shared drain line topology for the output stage, and achieves an output power density greater than 3 W/mm. Efficiency and thermal performance, namely peak junction temperature, have been signficantly improved compared to the predecessor design in [1] at both the MMIC and module levels, reducing DC power consumption by 40 W while maintaining RF output power in the same module.

articleTitle: Electrostatic Discharge Stress Effects on the Performance and Reliability of High Performance NPN SiGe HBTs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: We investigate the electrostatic discharge (ESD) stress effects on the performance and reliability of high performance NPN SiGe HBTs which are not designed to be part of an ESD protection scheme, but they may be subjected to residual ESD currents when connected to the IC input pin. Transmission line pulsing (TLP) measurements are conducted in NPNs of various emitter lengths and robust ESD tolerance is demonstrated. TLP testing results in a gradual increase of the forward bias base current which is found to correlate with the TLP stress current density and the device emitter length. Measurements and TCAD simulations provide insights into the physical mechanisms that drive the base current (Ib) increase during the ESD event. Two mechanisms responsible for the base current increase are observed; The first one increases the non- ideal recombination component of Ib and the second mechanism increases the ideal recombination component of Ib. Post-Tlpmeasurements indicate that the second component of Ib increase is largely recoverable. RF characterization results point to either no degradation or minimal degradation of the peak unity current gain frequency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{T}})$</tex>. Finally, we report for the first time, results from hot-carrier injection (HCI) stress experiments conducted on NPN SiGe HBTs that are first subjected to non-destructive TLP testing; The hot-carrier reliability of these ESD stressed devices is only marginally affected compared to the reliability of the pristine devices.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of Discrete Silicon Carbide Integrated Passive Devices in High-Power RF Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: The benefits of using discrete Silicon Carbide (SiC) integrated passive devices (IPDs) in the pre-match component of high-power RF amplifiers is examined. Through accurate modeling and simulation, the losses in both connected and unconnected passive components are correlated with the amplifier performance metrics such as efficiency and gain. A comparison of the losses in IPDs made on low-resistivity Silicon (Si) substrates show that gain and efficiency can be improved by substitution from Si to SiC IPDs. Both simulation and measured data on fabricated amplifier prototypes show a 2dB improvement in gain, and 2% improvement in efficiency at 3.8GHz and 85 W average output power for the amplifier product using SiC IPDs.

articleTitle: Advanced mHEMT Technologies for Use in Radar, Communication and Meteorological Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: Three sub-100 nm metamorphic high electron mobility transistor (mHEMT) technologies have been developed for use in next-generation radar, communication and meteorological applications at millimeter wave and submillimeter wave frequencies. The advanced mHEMT technologies feature a gate-length of 50, 35 and 20 nm in combination with a high In-content <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{In}_{0.80}\text{Ga}_{0.20}\text{As}$</tex> channel, thus enabling excellent extrinsic transit frequencies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\it fi}$</tex> up to 600 GHz and maximum oscillation frequencies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$fmm$</tex> of more than 1 THz. Based on these technologies, we could successfully realize a variety of ultra-broadband state of the art low-noise and power amplifiers as well as multifunctional transmitter and receiver circuits, demonstrating very low noise figure (NF = 1.7 dB @ 75–110 GHz), high output power (Pout> 10 mW @ 75–305 GHz) and high small-signal gain (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{21}=33\text{dB}$</tex> @ 730 GHz).

articleTitle: D-Band 4-ch Antenna-on-Chip Phased-Array TX Front-End
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: In this paper, we report a D-band phased-array TX front-end with 4 antenna elements on chip implemented in a 22-nm SOI-CMOS process. The TX front-end consists of a wideband vector synthesis phase shifter, power amplifier and antenna. The phase shifter has a gain of −7dB and is a switching-based digitally controlled phase shifter with excellent phase control stability over temperature. The power amplifier delivers 8.5 dBm output P1dB and 23 dB gain at 150 GHz. The antenna is realized on the chip with a tapered slot and radiates towards the edge of the chip. A D-band phased-array module equipped with four of these is realized on a single chip.

articleTitle: A 15–24 GHz, 15W Reactively Matched GaN MMIC Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: The design and measured performance of a reactively matched power amplifier (RMPA) operating from 15 to 24GHz and achieving an output power of 15W with an associated PAE between 19% and 31% is demonstrated. The RMPA outperformed a distributed PA design targeting the same goals, and is therefore presented in this work. The 3-stage circuit demonstrates high performance over a significant bandwidth (46%), covering much of Ku- and K-bands. Thermal analysis for this design demonstrates a peak junction temperature that is unacceptably high for many applications, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$343^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, along with a discussion about thermal improvements.

articleTitle: Simulation of DC Safe Operating Area and RF Breakdown in SiGe PA HBT
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents the simulation of DC safe operating area (SOA) and RF breakdown voltage in silicon germanium (SiGe) heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBT). High power HBTs engineered for advanced communications standards like 801.11ac and 801.11ax operate close to the SOA limit. DC and RF breakdown or ruggedness are therefore important considerations for power amplifier (PA) device and should be well characterized and simulated. It is shown that RF breakdown is directly correlated to DC SOA when both are measured under the base voltage bias mode. By modeling DC SOA well, RF breakdown voltage can be predicted with good accuracy. This is achieved by leveraging the improved strong avalanche breakdown current modeling at high injection levels in the HICUM/L2 v3.0 that is absent in v2.3x. The ability to accurately simulate DC SOA and RF breakdown are key features of a power amplifier model and allows the circuit designer to design for maximum output power and satisfy ruggedness criteria.

articleTitle: A 377–416 GHz Push-Push Frequency Doubler with Driving Stage and Transformer-Based Mode Separation in SiGe BiCMOS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents a WR2.2 push-push frequency doubler with two driving stages using Infineon's advanced 90nm SiGe BiCMOS technology, providing HBTs with an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{t}}/\mathrm{f}_{\max}$</tex> of 300 GHz/500 GHz, respectively. Compared to conventional push-push frequency doublers, we use a design that utilizes transformer-based mode separation. The architecture of the doubler is essentially that of a differential cascode amplifier with a transformer as the load. However, the center tap of the secondary side of the transformer is connected to the MMIC output, causing the second harmonic to be the largest component of the output signal. Measurements exhibit a 3 dB bandwidth of 39 GHz, covering the frequency range from 377 GHz to 416 GHz. The maximum conversion gain is 2.9 dB and the maximum measured output power equals -5.4dBm at 390 GHz.

articleTitle: A 28-Gb/s 27.2mW NRZ Full-Rate Bang-Bang Clock and Data Recovery in 22 nm FD-SOI CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents a 28-Gb/s full-rate NRZ bang-bang clock and data recovery (CDR) in 22 nm FD-SOI CMOS technology. In order to reduce supply voltage and power dis-sipation, class-AB current-mode logic (CML) and forward-body biasing (FBB) are extensively used. Furthermore, the clock driver and clock path in the bang-bang phase detector are carefully optimized. The circuit operates reliably in a wide range of supply voltages from 0.8 to 1.2 V without adjustment of the body biasing. The CDR core dissipates 27.2mW at 0.8V supply voltage and 54.4 mW at 1.2 V supply voltage. The recovered full-rate data surpasses jitter tolerance with a good margin (BER less than 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup>) over the entire supply voltage range. A figure-of-merit (FoM) of 0.97 mW/ Gb/s for 0.8 V supply voltage is achieved. This FoM represents the best FoM for full-rate NRZ bang-bang CDRs above 20 Gb/s and compares reasonably well with high-speed half-rate and quarter-rate NRZ CDR FoM<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex>.

articleTitle: Flipchip Characterization for RF SOI Switch Model Improvement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: Enhancing flipchip simulation accuracy is key to minimizing die spins to meet performance targets. This paper shows how characterization in a flipchip environment is key to improving RF SOI (silicon on insulator) switch models over on-wafer characterization. Characterizing the switch's coupling to ground is key in achieving simulation improvement.

articleTitle: Optimization of GaN HEMTs with ScAlN Barrier for High 2DEG Density and Low on-Resistance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: ScAlN is a novel barrier material for GaN-based high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs), with the potential to provide extremely high carrier densities and ultra-low on-resistance in RF and switching power supply applications. In this work, we simulate the density of two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG), electron mobility and on-resistance in GaN HEMT structures with a ScAlN barrier using an advanced mobility modeling framework. We outline the advantages of a ScAlN barrier device by comparing it to an AIGaN barrier HEMT, where we obtain a 2.44 times higher 2DEG sheet density and an improvement in on-resistance by a factor of 2.26. Thereafter, we optimize the barrier Sc-content and thickness to achieve a minimal room-temperature on-resistance of 130 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega/\square$</tex>, with a 2DEG density close to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5.10^{13} \ \text{cm}^{-2}$</tex>. Furthermore, we examine the impact of GaN and AlN interlayers (ILs), which are commonly added between the ScAlN barrier and GaN channel, and find that a thinner GaN IL and a thicker AlN IL is preferred for high 2DEG density and low on-resistance, provided that the strain-induced dislocations for AlN layers close to their critical thickness do not degrade the 2DEG mobility. The study reveals the most important factors determining the on-resistance, thereby offering guidance for the design of future ScAlN barrier HEMTs.

articleTitle: Low Phase Noise and Low Power Consumption Magnetic Cross-Coupled Push-Push VCO in SiGe BiCMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: Low phase noise VCO circuits with 80 GHz outputs are investigated and implemented in a SiGe BiCMOS technology. The newly developed magnetic cross-coupled VCO has achieved a VCO tuning range from 76.7 GHz to 85.3 GHz and the best phase noise of −104 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset frequency which is a record value for a single core VCO at the frequency range of 80 GHz, according to the best knowledge of the authors. This VCO chip consumes a DC current of 79 mA which includes the VCO core current consumption of approximately 19 mA at a supply voltage of 3.3 V with a complete chip area of 2.1 sq. mm while the VCO core area is 0.27 sq. mm. A capacitive cross-coupled VCO has also been designed for comparison. It has achieved a tuning range from 78 GHz to 85.4 GHz and the best phase noise of −102.1 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset frequency. This VCO chip consumes a DC current of 100 mA from a 3.3 V supply which includes the VCO core current consumption of approximately 37 mA.

articleTitle: A Compact 0.98 THz Source With On-Chip Antenna In 250-nm InP DHBT
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents a lensless THz source with on-chip antenna in 250-nm DHBT. The proposed topology consists of a push-push oscillator with an extremely compact coupled-line based common-base core. The source achieves a peak EIRP and output power of -14 dBm and -19.5 dBm respectively at 966 GHz. The output frequency is tunable from 960 GHz to 990 GHz and the peak DC-RF efficiency is 0.028 %. To the authors best knowledge, this is the highest operating frequency reported in a push-push oscillator in any IC process.

articleTitle: A Ka-Band VCO Chip with Integrated Dividers Using 1.5 V Supply in 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS Technology for Low-Power Radar Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: High-frequency LO signal generation blocks take away significant amount of the power budget in radar sensors. The ever increasing demand for highly efficient and battery powered portable applications require low-voltage and low-power oscillators and frequency dividers. This paper presents the design and characterization results of a low-power SiGe BiCMOS VCO chip with integrated dividers at Ka-band which operates with a single supply voltage of only 1.5 V still having key performance parameters meeting the modern radar application needs. Despite the limited voltage range the resonant circuit in the Colpitts oscillator core is optimized to provide 2.5 GHz of analog tuning bandwidth. A transformer based Miller compensated amplifier is used as the output buffer to have 6.3 dBm of differential power at 32.8 GHz while the total dc power consumption of the LO signal generation circuits is 27 mW. The integrated divide-by-16 signal chain followed by a two-stage buffer consumes 44 mW providing 0 dBm differential output power sufficient to drive an external PLL. Experimental results confirm that the proposed chip with wide continuous tuning range and integrated low-voltage dividers is promising for highly efficient low-power radar sensors.

articleTitle: A 12 Bit R-2R Digital-to-Analog Converter for Shuttling Operation in a Trapped-Ion Quantum Computer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This work presents a 12 bit, resistive R-2R ladder-based Digital-to-Analog Converter (DAC) intended to generate arbitrary waveforms for shuttling operation in a trapped-ion quantum computer (TIQC) using 171 Yb + ions. The DAC operates at a sampling frequency of 1 MHz and can replicate constant, sinusoidal, rectangular, and triangular signals within a full-scale (FS) range of ±0.9V and a resolution of 500 μV. To mitigate ion shaking in the trap, a low pass filter minimizes glitch errors at major output code transitions and a spectral noise density (SND) of 45.3nV/VHz has been measured at 100 kHz. Implemented in a 130 nm high-voltage (HV) bulk CMOS technology, the DAC consumes 1.1 m W from a 1.5 V power supply at room temperature (RT). This includes a reference buffer and a serial peripheral interface (SPI) to read in the DAC control words. The whole circuitry takes up an active area of 1200 x 700 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> excluding pads. Due to its small area, low power consumption and excellent noise performance, the DAC is ideally suited as the core building block for an ion shuttling controller IC.

articleTitle: Quad-Channel 100-GHz-Bandwidth InP- HBT-Based Linear Amplifier Module for High Symbol Rate Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: We have developed a quad-channel baseband linear amplifier module with four distributed amplifier ICs using our in-house indium-phosphide hetero-junction bipolar transistor (InP HBT) technology. A new push-on connector interface integrating the quad-channel is utilized to achieve miniaturization and high integration. The module has a bandwidth of 100 GHz, and all four channels exhibit uniform characteristics. In addition to the uniform frequency characteristics, the linear amplification functions are observed in all channels at the speed of 112-GBaud PAM4 (224 Gb/s). To the best of our knowledge, this is the world's first 100-GHz-bandwidth linear amplifier module with four channels integrated.

articleTitle: A Shunt-Feedback TIA with Common-Base Variable Gain Input Stage for 128-GBaud Coherent Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: We present a fully differential linear transimpedance amplifier − (TIA) with a common-base (CB) variable gain circuit as the input stage of a shunt-feedback (SFB) TIA circuit. A quad channel TIA chip is fabricated in 55-nm SiGe BiCMOS technology, and shows measured transimpedance gain of 70 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{dB}\Omega,$</tex> 42-dB gain dynamic range, and 80-GHz bandwidth. An intradyne coherent receiver (ICR) with this TIA shows measured result of greater than 75-GHz bandwidth of O/E response. To the authors' knowledge, this is the highest bandwidth among the reported differential TIAs with the variable gain function. An experimental transmission evaluation of 128-GBaud single polarization 16 quadrature amplitude modulation (SP-16QAM) is implemented and an error vector magnitude (EVM) of 13.2% is observed.

articleTitle: On Extracting the Maximum Power Density at High Frequencies from Gallium Nitride and Related Materials
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: The demand for higher power density in electronic applications has made Gallium Nitride HEMT technology a front-runner in both power and RF applications due to its exceptional material properties. However, to fully unleash GaN's potential, thermal management is crucial to address the issue of severe Joule heating causing performance degradation and premature failure. A potential solution lies in integrating diamond, known for its excellent thermal properties, with GaN HEMTs. Although diamond growth on GaN has been challenging, a recent breakthrough in our group has demonstrated successful diamond-on-GaN integration using a low-temperature growth process <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\sim 400^{\circ}\mathrm{C})$</tex>. The integrated diamond films showed high thermal conductivity (300 W/m/K) and phase purity (97%), resulting in significantly reduced peak temperature in GaN HEMT channel by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$> 100^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> during operation at 20 W/ mm. This advancement opens up new possibilities for improving the efficiency and performance of GaN-based electronics.

articleTitle: A 33 dBm, >30% PAE GaN Power Amplifier Based on a Sub-Quarter-Wavelength Balun for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: In this paper, a two-stage Ka-band power amplifier (PA) utilizing a sub-quarter-wavelength (SQWL) balun is presented for efficient and compact series power combining. The differential two-stage PA includes a high-order interstage matching network to suppress AM-PM distortion without the addition of additional active devices. The PA is fabricated using a 150nm GaN technology and produces over 32 dB<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> output power across a frequency range of 26–30 GHz. The differential pair plus SQWL balun occupies a small area of only 0.4mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, resulting in a high power density of 5.725 W/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>• The presented PA is among the highest in power & efficiency achieved with a differential-end PA at Ka-band frequency range in G<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex>N technologies.

articleTitle: Single-Ended Resistive Down-Converter MMICs in InGaAs mHEMT and GaN-HEMT Technologies for D-Band (110–170 GHz) Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper reports on the comparison done for the first time between the simulations and measurements of monolithic millimeter-wave integrated single-ended passive down-converter circuits, fabricated in the 35-nm and 50-nm gate-length mHEMT technologies, and in the 100-nm gate-length AlGaN/GaN HEMT technology. The down-converters are intended for operation in D-band (110–170 GHz). The three MMICs are based on a single-ended resistive-type mixer with a single transistor topology and give an IF output frequency of 200 MHz. The average measured conversion gain of the 35-nm and 50-nm mHEMT mixer is −6.5 dB and −7.5 dB, respectively, driven by an LO input power of 4 dBm. The measured 1-dB compression point is more than 6 dBm of RF input power for both circuits. The average conversion gain of the 100-nm GaN-HEMT mixer is −9.6 dB with an LO power of 11 dBm and its 1-dB compression point is greater than 7 dBm.

articleTitle: Monolithic Silicon Photonics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper details a monolithic approach to the integration of photonic systems. Polarization diverse photonic components are fabricated in a 45nm silicon-on-insulator microelectronics process flow which includes digital and RFCMOS, high performance analog mixed signal, mmWave components, electro-thermal and electro-optic control elements, and fiber and laser attach. This results in a single chip optical transceiver solution.

articleTitle: Cryogenic Modeling for Open-Source Process Design Kit Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: Models and design guidelines for silicon complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) devices operating at cryogenic temperatures are needed due to a recent spike in interest in cryogenic applications, ranging from quantum computing to readout integrated circuits. Demanding readout integrated circuit (IC) and quantum computing applications require highly reliable and complex CMOS circuitry operating well and reliably at low temperatures, such as 4K and 77K. In the case of quantum computing, Silicon (Si) CMOS circuits may need to work in a 4K ambient, or in an ambient with a temperature even lower than this. To enable circuit design, and demonstrate designs achievable with finetuned models at 4K, we measure and SPICE-type compact model CMOS devices from the 130nm Skywater technology node, at the ubiquitously used quantum computing temperature of 4K. This 130nm process is the open-source process design kit technology, currently being offered by Google and Skywater. The goal of this work is to pave the way to democratize circuit design in this niche region of operation for users of an open-foundry process such as this 130nm node, by providing standard SPICE compatible cryogenic device models. Additionally, we demonstrate the design of a two-stage amplifier circuit working at 4K developed utilizing the developed cryogenic models.

articleTitle: Adaptable 40 nm GaN T-Gate MMIC Processes for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: Aggressively scaled gallium nitride (GaN) high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) technologies with 40 nm T-gate lengths and extremely scaled ohmic-regrowth source-drain lengths ranging from 1500 nm to 150 nm comprise the low-loss, high-performance active devices in advanced high-power and high-efficiency monolithic microwave integrated circuits (MMICs). This paper outlines the latest device, circuit, and foundry access of three commercially available 40 nm GaN T-gate MMIC processes for millimeter-wave applications.

articleTitle: A Circuit Designer's Perspective on Transistor Modelling Challenges for 6G, Fiberoptics, and Quantum Computing ICs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper reviews how HBT and FET compact models should be effectively used in the initial design of mm-wave 6G and fiberoptics circuits above 100 GHz and suggests which high frequency core model parameters and RCL parasitics require refinements. The latter are in part limited by on-die transistor S-parameter measurement and de-embedding inaccuracies at J-Band. Finally, we discuss the compact model research challenges that remain in capturing optimal noise figure current density and quantum phenomena at cryogenic temperatures, and the numerical convergence issues observed in existing commercial SiGe BiCMOS and CMOS process design kits below 20 K.

articleTitle: Comparative Performance of 100–200 GHz Wideband Transceivers: CMOS vs Compound Semiconductors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper provides a survey of silicon bulk CMOS, FD-SOI, SOI, and SiGe transceivers and compares their performance to compound semiconductor implementations in III-V technology nodes. A comparison of transistor level, block level, and complete transceiver level performance is presented to gauge the applicability of CMOS technology to these emerging higher frequency communication and sensing applications.

articleTitle: Electro-Thermal Investigation of SiGe HBTs: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents a review on the electro-thermal investigation of SiGe HBT technologies. After introducing a simple method of measuring thermal resistance (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf>), analytical studies on the calculation of R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf> is discussed and subsequently the contribution of the back-end-of-line metal lines is estimated. Based on this analysis, strategies for the optimum emitter finger placements while designing a power amplifier cell are investigated. Finally, the thermal impedance measurement and modelling aspects are discussed.

articleTitle: Practical and Efficient Approaches to Device Modeling and Power Amplifier Module Design
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: A 'best-practices' approach to device modeling and power amplifier (PA) module design optimization is described. It was developed to help designers go from the arrival of footprint and electrical specs to samples-out as fast and accurately as possible. It uses the same modulation signals and average output powers as on the lab measurement benches, properly averages the spec'd quantities (Gain, ACPR, EVM, PAE, IRL,..), and covers the full frequency band. Designing the module involves organizing the simulation output into a single weighted and normalized figure of merit that the optimizer can use as its one-goal error function. This FOM also serves as a meaningful progress monitor, and design-review quality measure. Waveform engineering and gain curve shaping are not explicitly part of the process, but happen ‘under the hood’, automatically, in a properly weighted and averaged way. Physically based and physically scalable (geometrically and thermally) active device models (GaAs HBT and PHEMT) serve as the foundation of the approach, with more emphasis on adherence to known and manageable temperature-dependent device physics than perfect snap-shot model-measurement agreement. Such models are not subor-dinates to the semiconductor fabrication process and measured data, but can help improve the former and monitor the latter. It allows for meaningful investigations of device structure variations and product yield, and promotes accuracy in circuit envelope (CE) and electrothermal (ETh) simulations. The optimization is done with harmonic balance (HB) and S-parameter (SP) simulation data. The setup incorporates envelope tracking (ET) and digital predistortion (DPD) in an efficient way.

articleTitle: AlScN High Electron Mobility Transistors: Integrating High Piezoelectric, High K Dielectric, and Ferroelectric Functionality
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents an overview of the promising physical properties of the aluminum scandium nitride (AlScN) ternary alloy system and its integration in radiofrequency heterostructure high electron mobility transistors (RF HEMTs). Specifically, heterostructures with AlScN demonstrate enhanced piezoelectric response and enhanced relative dielectric permittivity, as well as ferroelectric behavior. These promising physical phenomena are manifested in HEMTs that show larger on current densities compared to aluminum gallium nitride (AlGaN) HEMTs and display ferroelectric behavior. An overlook on future improvements in thin film deposition and device fabrication is discussed to fully maximize the potential devices and integrated circuits incorporating AlScN.
